message:
I couldn't run a quick sanity test (`python3 -c ...`) — this session has no approval surface for Bash, so the command was auto-denied. The implementation itself is in place:

```python
def slugify(title: str, max_length: int = 60) -> str:
    normalized = unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", title)
    ascii_only = normalized.encode("ascii", "ignore").decode("ascii")
    lowered = ascii_only.lower()
    slug = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]+", "-", lowered).strip("-")
    slug = slug[:max_length].strip("-")
    return slug
```

It NFKD-normalizes to split accented characters into base+combining marks, drops non-ASCII (stripping accents, e.g. `é` → `e`), lowercases, collapses runs of non-alphanumerics into a single `-`, trims leading/trailing `-`, then truncates to `max_length` and re-trims any trailing `-` left by the cut. Only stdlib (`re`, `unicodedata`) is used, per the file's note. Let me know if you'd like me to verify it once you can run the command.
